newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-NZ CAPTAIN ACCEPTS STOMPING ACCIDENTAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NZ CAPTAIN ACCEPTS STOMPING ACCIDENTAL.

text.p: All Black captain Sean Fitzpatrick said on Monday he accepted that Springbok flanker Andre Venter had not intentionally stomped on his face in Saturday's Tri-Nations rugby test.

"I haven't seen the incident on TV yet. I don't know if it was intentional or not. I know Andre and we spoke after the game. He said it wasn't intentional, so I accept that," Fitzpatrick told National Radio.

Venter received the first red card of the Tri-Nations series and became only the third Springbok ever to be sent from the field when he stomped on Fitzpatrick's head as he lay trapped at the bottom of a ruck.
Venter was suspended from rugby for three weeks by a judicial committee of organising body SANZAR on Sunday. The committee found him guilty of reckless stomping.
Reduced to 14 men, the Springboks went on to suffer their heaviest ever defeat by an All Black side, losing Saturday's match by a record 20-point margin, 35-55.
Fitzpatrick said the Springboks' lack of discipline had cost them the match.
"They lost their way and resorted to ill-discipline to make their point ... and consequently lost the game," he said.
"The successful teams are the ones that are very disciplined and can control themselves in those situations. It's a contact sport and things happen that you have to control yourself in."
The All Black captain said the South Africans were guilty of more than one unsporting incident during the tense game that did not belong on the rugby field.

"There's things that went on that I don't like to see in a game. Lots of continuous niggle and off-the-ball play -- after the ball's gone they're standing on your legs, punches and things like that which you don't need. You just need to get on with the game," he said.
The stomping revived memories of the infamous attack on Fitzpatrick by another Springbok, Johan le Roux, in 1994. Le Roux was sent home in disgrace after he bit the ear of the All Black skipper.
But Fitzpatrick rejected the suggestion he has been targeted by the Springboks.
"I don't think so. I think I'm just at the wrong place at the right time. I've just been caught at the bottom of a few rucks."
Fitzpatrick, who led the All Blacks for the 50th time in tests on Saturday, said he had enjoyed the match despite the brutal play, which saw more than one player leave the field bloodied and bruised.
"It's disappointing that the focus has been on Andre Venter, when it would have been nice to focus on some of the good things.
"For us they're the world champions and before Saturday they were our greatest challenge. To beat them by that score like we did on Saturday, I would never have thought that possible.
"It was nice to finally beat them so convincingly."
